description: Course introduction, logistics, and an initial overview of expressions and call expressions; includes example Python script exploring values and simple programs.
Basics of functions, assignment statements, environment diagrams, and multiple assignment with supporting Python examples.
Control structures including conditional statements and while loops, with algorithmic examples like prime factorization and digit processing.
Functions as arguments and return values, DRY principles, and examples demonstrating higher-order function design.
Environment diagrams, currying, lambda expressions, and higher-order function patterns with exercises.
Introduction to recursion: base cases, recursive calls, and converting iterative solutions to recursive ones.
Tree recursion patterns, combinatorial counting problems, and recursive problem-solving strategies.
List comprehensions, recursive list processing, and sequence manipulation techniques.
Data abstraction principles and tree ADTs, including dictionary comprehensions and tree implementations.
List mutation, identity vs equality, and mutable recursive data structures with examples and exercises.
Iterators, generators, map usage, and generator-based approaches to combinatorial problems.
Review of core topics (recursion, generators, environment diagrams, tree manipulation) for the midterm.
Introduction to object-oriented programming: classes, attributes, methods, and attribute lookup semantics.
Class inheritance, attribute resolution, and object string representations with practical class exercises.
Mutable tree data structures, string representations, and algorithms that mutate trees.
Linked list structure and class implementation, with recursive and iterative processing examples.
Algorithmic efficiency, orders of growth, and practical performance demonstrations (notebook + code).
Introduction to Scheme: syntax, evaluation model, lambda expressions, and linked list manipulation.
Scheme list construction and list-processing techniques, including special forms and symbolic programming examples.
Tail-call optimization, space-efficient recursion, and related Scheme evaluation concepts.
Introduction to relational databases and SQL: tables, SELECT, joins, aliases, and example queries.
SQL aggregation, GROUP BY, joins, and practical database query exercises.
Foundational theoretical computer science topics: complexity, computability, reductions, and P vs NP.
